title: Update runtime benchmarking harness for FP8/INT8 kernel modes + reproducible measurement
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
- We’re benchmarking FP8 and INT8 kernel paths (microbench + end-to-end) across H100/A100 (and L4 where applicable). Current harness is good for baseline BF16/FP16 comparisons but lacks:
  (1) explicit FP8/INT8 modes with correctness checks
  (2) stable warmup/measurement rules that reduce variance
  (3) standardized shape sweeps that match top hosted model regimes
  (4) artifact metadata sufficient for reproducibility (driver/CUDA, clocks, git SHA, model hash, config)

Scope
1) Add quantized modes
- Add CLI/config toggles for kernel_mode: baseline | fp8 | int8
- Ensure the harness can run both microbench (kernel timing) and end-to-end serving benchmarks under the same mode flag
- Add guardrails so unsupported shapes/modes fall back with an explicit, machine-readable reason (not silent)

2) Standardize warmup + measurement
- Warmup: fixed number of iterations AND a minimum wall-time requirement (to avoid short-run jitter)
- Measurement: fixed run count, with per-run timing samples retained (not only aggregates)
- Enforce consistent prefill/decode splits in end-to-end runs and capture TTFT/TPOT separately

3) Shape sweeps (representative)
- Provide a default shape suite aligned to the “top hosted models” families (hidden size/head dim regimes) and typical seq-len distributions
- Include both prefill-dominant and decode-heavy cases
- Include batch size / concurrency sweeps where applicable

4) Artifact export + metadata
- Emit structured artifacts per run (JSON) plus a summary index for matrix aggregation
- Attach metadata: git SHA, container tag, CUDA, driver, GPU name + MIG/partitioning, clock lock status, model revision/hash, kernel_mode, batch/concurrency, seq-lens, and hostname/node id
- Output should be upload-friendly for Drive/warehouse usage

Acceptance criteria (DoD)
- Harness supports kernel_mode=fp8 and kernel_mode=int8 end-to-end (no manual patches) and baseline remains unchanged
- Warmup and measurement logic is unified and applied consistently across microbench and e2e modes
- Default shape suite exists and is runnable as a single command; produces per-shape results + aggregates
- Artifacts include required metadata fields and can be aggregated by benchmark-lab runner without custom parsing
- Variance improvement: on H100, repeated baseline runs for a single representative case show <3% relative stddev for tokens/s and <5% for TTFT (after clock pinning is enabled); if not achieved, harness must log a ‘variance_warning’ and capture the suspected cause (clocks unlocked, thermal throttling, shared node)
- Documentation: README/usage docs updated with examples and “known sources of noise” section

Non-goals
- Choosing the final kernel auto-selection heuristics (tracked in ENG-7430 / ADR-019)
- Implementing perf canary gating (ENG-7426)

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Rina Kobayashi
- Contributors: Isabella Rossi (microbench harness), Grace Kim (FP8/INT8 coverage)
- Reviewers: Noah Patel (perf rigor), Claire Dubois (methodology)

Rollout plan
- Land harness changes behind non-default flags; existing CI perf runs continue using baseline mode
- Validate on a single H100 node first, then widen to A100; once stable, enable for matrix runs (ENG-7428)

Notes
- Known issues we’ve seen in prior runs: debug logging perturbing timing, driver mismatches across clusters, and clock drift/thermal throttling. Harness should surface these explicitly in metadata + warnings rather than letting them silently affect results.
comments: 2026-02-10 (Talia Benson): Marking this as P0 for the sprint. We’re blocked on credible results until harness can do FP8/INT8 with reproducible rules + metadata. Please keep changes minimally invasive to baseline path; we need to avoid breaking existing perf suite consumers.

2026-02-11 (Rina Kobayashi): Drafted implementation plan: (a) add kernel_mode plumbed end-to-end, (b) unify warmup/measure loop into a shared utility, (c) add shape suite YAML + generator for common regimes, (d) emit artifact JSON per case. Pulling Isabella in for microbench parity.

2026-02-12 (Isabella Rossi): Microbench currently times kernels with CUDA events but e2e uses wall timers + histograms. Suggest we keep CUDA-event timing for microbench but standardize output schema + per-iter samples. For e2e, keep TTFT/TPOT histograms but ensure fixed warmup and run counts.

2026-02-13 (Noah Patel): Please ensure we always tag: model_id/model_hash, kernel registry name + version, and whether fallback happened. Without that, we can’t trust comparisons. Also: include a ‘measurement_window_ms’ field so we can reason about sampling noise.

2026-02-15 (Rina Kobayashi): Opened PR for harness changes and FP8/INT8 toggles. Added ‘variance_warning’ when clocks not locked and a check for mixed driver/CUDA versions. Still need to finalize shape suite defaults (waiting on top hosted models list confirmation).

2026-02-16 (Grace Kim): Added initial shape list for 3 regimes: small (L4-ish), medium (A100 common), large (H100 common). Need to cross-check head_dim=64/128 variants for attention kernels. Also propose adding a decode-heavy suite with small batch/high concurrency to reflect chat traffic.

2026-02-18 (Claire Dubois): Review feedback: warmup should be both fixed iters AND min time to avoid preemption artifacts. Also ensure we log GPU clock lock state (requested vs effective) + temps if available. For claims, we need raw run samples retained.

2026-02-20 (Rina Kobayashi): Updated PR with min warmup time + per-run samples retained. Added artifact metadata fields per review. Confirmed baseline path output unchanged except for additional metadata fields (non-breaking).

2026-02-21 (Sofia Ivanova): Please coordinate with ENG-7425 instrumentation so e2e harness can emit prefill/decode breakdown consistently. Even if not required for this ticket, we should avoid schema churn later.

2026-02-24 (Rina Kobayashi): Merged. Harness now supports kernel_mode=fp8/int8, standardized warmup/measurement, default shape suite, and structured artifacts. Next: matrix execution (ENG-7428) + ensure runner pins clocks/driver (benchmark-lab PRs).
